won.source: The fed's own title history (SWF Raw), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: The third Outlawz member to hold the title, beating T-Money at one of the final SWF events.
note: The title history then shows the title vacant while the SWF was closed for six months.

title: chz-hardcore
label: The Count

won.source: The fed's own title history (SWF Inferno), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: Destroyed T-Money in a Transylvania Hardkore match.

title: chz-hardcore
label: JT Fringe

won.source: The fed's own title history (SWF PPV Psycho Circus), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: Escaped a Transylvania Hardkore match with The Count after a blast from a fire extinguisher.
note: The title history's own footnote: Fringe relinquished the title on winning the SWF Heavyweight Title.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Don Rossi

won.source: The fed's own title history (SWF Inferno), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: Pinned Barbwire with the Game Over in a triple threat with Havoc.
note: Rossi's own roster card says he won the SWF Hardcore belt "from Havoc".

title: chz-hardcore
label: The Count

won.source: The fed's own title history (SWF PPV Total Chaos), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: Escaped a triple threat with unexpected help from Thor.
note: The title history's own footnote: The Count was kept as a non-fighting champion until a final could be held in the new CHZ.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Diablo

won.source: The fed's own title history (CHZ WILD), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: Beat his friend and partner Fire.
note: The 21 September 2001 Friday Night Wild stages the win and bills it "for the right to be the First Hardcore Champion", calling Diablo "the first ever CHZ hardcore champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/fnw-2001-09-21.html); the fed's own title history instead has The Count holding the belt from 1 April 2001 until that night.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Extreme Chancelz

won.source: The fed's own title history (CHZ WILD), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: Beat his Team Extreme stablemate Diablo for his first CHZ title.

lost.source: The 23 January 2002 Wednesday Night Wild, where Black Dragon beats him for the title (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-01-23.html). The fed's own title history dates the loss 1/24/02 (/promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html).

note: Won in a four-way barbed wire match on the 14 November 2001 house show in Halifax (the fed's own title history names the event a Wild). Retains against Violent Dave on 12 December 2001 in a bathroom-and-loading-dock brawl, ending when a tipped forklift drops both men to the concrete (promotions/chz/archive/wild-2001-12-12.html); still champion on the fed's own 22 December 2001 snapshot ten days later (promotions/chz/archive/champions-2001.html). Lost to Black Dragon on 24 January 2002.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Black Dragon

won.source: The 23 January 2002 Wednesday Night Wild, where Black Dragon pins Extreme Chancelz in the parking lot: "We have a NEW CHZ HARDCORE CHAMPION!!!!" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-01-23.html). The fed's own title history dates the win 1/24/02 (/promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html).

how: Back after six months away, upset Extreme Chancelz in his second match.
note: Sources disagree by a day: the fed's own title history dates the win 24 January 2002, and the 23 January 2002 Wild stages it; the reign follows the broadcast, and the history's date is kept in the source.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Lucifer

won.source: The fed's own title history (CHZ PPV No Luv), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html. The 27 February 2002 No Luv script stages the win: a fisherman brain buster pin on Black Dragon, "NEW CHZ HARDCORE CHAMPION……..LUCIFER!!" (/promotions/chz/archive/no-luv-2002-02-27.html).

how: Bested The Count and Black Dragon at the February pay-per-view.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Madd Maxx

won.source: The fed's own title history (CHZ WILD), /promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html.

how: Won "a killer match" for his first CHZ Hardcore Title.
note: Billed defending against Wild Dog and Lucifer in a triple threat at the unaired NBK Pride — no result survives anywhere held. Not involved in the hardcore-rules (non-title) Wild Dog vs. Hell's Keeper match on 22 March 2002.

title: chz-television
label: Rage

won.source: Beats Chris Mathews via ankle lock submission on 22 March 2002, after Mathews escapes a sharpshooter (promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-03-22.html).

how: Submission (ankle lock), in a full, clean, fully-scripted match.
note: Billed defending against Galuda at the unaired NBK Pride — no result survives anywhere held.

title: chz-world-heavyweight
label: Jake Schultz

won.source: Mind Games, the CHZ's 2002 pay-per-view: "HE DID IT! JAKE SCHULTZ IS THE CHZ WORLD CHAMPION!" (/promotions/chz/archive/mind-games-2002-08-31.html).

how: Won the vacant title, billed "the Canuck Heat Zone World Heavyweight Championship", by powerbombing Matt Hunt through a table in a barbed wire tables match at Mind Games; the fed crowned him its first World Heavyweight Champion of the 2002 relaunch.

lost.source: The fed's own sale announcement of 11 September 2002, in which the new owner strips all champions of their titles (/promotions/chz/archive/front-page-2002-09.html); the champions page lists the title vacant (/promotions/chz/archive/champions-2002-09.html).

note: The first reign of the belt the fed's June 2002 relaunch listed with no champions (title-history-2002.html) and as vacant with the contenders to be announced (champions-2002-06.html): the fed's own front page of 11 September 2002 asks "who would be crowned the first CHZ World Heavyweight Champion?" (front-page-2002-09.html) and the Mind Games broadcast says "A very first CHZ Champion will be crowned". Sources disagree: the fed's own news item of 5 September 2002 says Matt Hunt "lost the brutal Barbed Wire Tables Match and the CHZ World Title in the process" (news-2002-09.html), though the broadcast crowns Schultz the first champion.

title: chz-tag-team-2002
label: Redemption Song

won.source: The team's own 2002 roster card, "CHZ Tag-Team Champions (14th A[ugust])" (/promotions/chz/archive/roster-card-2002-redemption.html); the 21 August 2002 Wild calls them "the newly crowned tag champs Redemption Song who defeated The Flying Vergomovs last week" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-08-21.html). The fed's own archived results of the 14 August 2002 Wild, in the same site backup, stage the tournament final

how: Beat the Flying Vergomovs in the falls-count-anywhere final of the tag team title tournament.

lost.source: The fed's own news of 2 September 2002: after the no contest at Mind Games, "it was declared the Tag Team Titles would become vacant", Redemption Song moving on from the CHZ (/promotions/chz/archive/news-2002-09.html).

note: The first reign of the belt the fed's June 2002 relaunch listed with no champions (title-history-2002.html) and as vacant with the contenders to be announced (champions-2002-06.html); the 21 August 2002 Wild calls Redemption Song "The newly crowned tag champs Redemption Song who defeated The Flying Vergomovs last week". Kept the titles on 21 August 2002 against Gold Rush; the Mind Games cage match against the Mystery Assailants ended in a no contest.

title: chz-national
label: Xander Crave

won.source: The fed's own archived results of the 7 August 2002 Wild, in the operator's own site backup ("We have a new National Champion in Xander Crave!"). The 21 August 2002 Wild bills him "the CHZ National Champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-08-21.html).

how: Beat Logan Cage in the final of the National Title tournament.

lost.source: The fed's own sale announcement of 11 September 2002, in which the new owner strips all champions of their titles (/promotions/chz/archive/front-page-2002-09.html); the champions page lists the title vacant (/promotions/chz/archive/champions-2002-09.html).

note: Kept the title against Tyler Van Serio on 21 August 2002 and against Logan Cage in a knockout match at Mind Games.

title: chz-womens
label: Xstacy

won.source: The belt's first match, for a golden thong made for the event: "Xstacy becomes the Women's Champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/breakout-2002-12-18.html).

how: Beat Misty Helms with Mad Max's help.

lost.source: Commissioner Inferno, hit by the belt when Xstacy swings it at Sai, takes it from her: "you have just been STRIPPED of the title for assaulting a CHZ official" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-04-23.html).

title: chz-womens
label: Sai

won.source: Sai beats Misty Helms for the vacant belt with the Double STF: "WE have a new Women's Champion... SAI!!!" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

how: Beat Misty Helms with the Double STF, the Widow's Web, with Dynamo Dragon at ringside.

title: chz-omega
label: The Inferno

won.source: The TLC cage match for the belt: "Inferno Wins the Omega Championship" (/promotions/chz/archive/breakout-2002-12-18.html).

how: Beat Lucifer in a TLC cage match by taking the belt off its strap; the booth calls the title one carried over to the CHZ from the LOW.

lost.source: Wild Dog is declared Omega Champion on 26 March 2003; the held shows do not show how Inferno's reign ended.

title: chz-omega
label: Wild Dog

won.source: Wild Dog's Big Bite beats Gus Theo: "that one move just declared The Wild Dog, the Omega Champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html).

how: Beat Gus Theo with the Big Bite in one move.

lost.source: The 14 May 2003 pay-per-view calls the Omega title vacant (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html); the held shows do not show the change.

note: Kept the title on 9 April 2003 when the Elimination Chamber match against Lucifer ended in a disqualification.

title: chz-omega
label: Wild Dog

won.source: The ladder match for the vacant Omega title: "What a win by Wild Dog!" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

how: Won the vacant title in a ladder match against Chazy 2 Cool, with Rage interfering.

title: chz-alpha
label: Don "The Game" Rossi

won.source: Rossi beats Chazy 2 Cool by submission in The Boss under the heading "Alpha title" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html).

how: Beat Chazy 2 Cool by submission in The Boss.

lost.source: The Darkness beats Rossi for the Alpha title (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

note: The write-up's closing line calls Rossi the Omega Champion under its Alpha title heading. He defended without a result against Rob Lewis on 23 April 2003.

title: chz-alpha
label: The Darkness

won.source: The Darkness pins Rossi: "NEW ALPHA CHAMPION, DARKNEEEEEEEEESS!" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

how: Beat Don Rossi after the referee's count, with a robed figure stunning Rossi.

lost.source: He hands the belt to the robed figure in the ring after the match (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

note: Handed the belt to Rage in the ring after the match.

title: chz-alpha
label: Rage

won.source: Keyser Soze unhoods the robed figure and names "your new NBK Alpha Champion... RAAAAAAAGE!" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

how: Handed the belt by the Darkness after the Darkness beat Don Rossi.
note: Carries the belt on 21 May 2003, when Rossi beats him in an impromptu match that is not for it.

title: chz-alpha
label: Harry Manback

won.source: BreakOut 2002 opens with footage of Manback "winning the Alpa Title" and closes on "The CHZ Alpha Champion Harry Manback" (/promotions/chz/archive/breakout-2002-12-18.html).

how: Alpha Champion at BreakOut 2002; the win is shown only in footage.

lost.source: Don Rossi wins the Alpha Championship on 26 March 2003; the held shows do not show how Manback's reign ended.

title: chz-north-american
label: Rob Lewis

won.source: The Last Call and the three count: "LEWIS IS THE NEW CHZ NORTH AMERICAN CHAMPION!!" (/promotions/chz/archive/breakout-2002-12-18.html).

how: Beat Don Rossi with the Last Call.

lost.source: Lucifer is billed as the North American champion on 5 March 2003 (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-05.html); the held shows do not show the change.

title: chz-north-american
label: Lucifer

won.source: The 5 March 2003 Wild bills "Bloodlust Vs Lucifer - North American Title", and the stand-in for the champion walks out to Lucifer's 'Breaking Me Down' by Soil as the crowd is "awaiting the North American champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-05.html); the held shows do not show how he won it after Rob Lewis's win of 18 December 2002.

how: Champion by 5 March 2003, when he does not come to work for his billed defence against Bloodlust and two stand-ins wrestle in its place.

lost.source: Keyser Soze has the title by the 26 March 2003 Wild, where the booth says he "has defaced the North American Title" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html); the held shows do not show the change.

note: Lucifer's entrance music is 'Breaking Me Down' by Soil on 26 March, 2 April and 9 April 2003.

title: chz-north-american
label: Keyser Soze

won.source: "Keyser Soze has defaced the North American Title" at the 26 March 2003 Wild (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html).

how: Champion by 26 March 2003, when his defence against the Reaper ends with no result.
note: Lost a defence to Chris Holler by count out on 9 April 2003 and kept the title; a defence against Drayton MacPhereson on 23 April ended with no winner; calls it "my North American title" on 14 May.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Lucifer

won.source: Lucifer pins Mad Max with the Apocalypse: "Lucifer is the NEW CHZ HARDCORE CHAMPION!" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html).

how: Beat Mad Max in a hardcore match through the arena.

lost.source: Xear defends the Hardcore Championship on 23 April 2003; the held shows do not show how Lucifer lost it.

note: Defended against Brendan Heaney on 2 April 2003 and kept the title by disqualification against Wild Dog on 9 April.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Zen Kyosaku

won.source: The three-way against Xear and Crimson Lord: "the new CHZ Hardcore champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

how: Won a three-way against Xear and Crimson Lord with a flying leg lariat and a standing moonsault.
note: Defended against Vladitor Pfister The Third on 21 May 2003.

title: chz-hardcore
label: Xear

won.source: Xear is "still Hardcore champion" when he defends against Chris Holler on 23 April 2003 (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-04-23.html).

how: Champion by 23 April 2003, when he beat Chris Holler in a hardcore match.

lost.source: Zen Kyosaku pins him in a three-way: "the new CHZ Hardcore champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

title: chz-tag-team
label: The Midnight Wonders

won.source: The 13 March 2002 Wednesday Night Wild's four corners elimination match for the vacant Tag Team Titles: "We have new tag team champs" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-03-13.html). The fed's own title history dates the win 3/18/02 (/promotions/chz/archive/tag-team-title-history.html).

how: Beat three other teams in a four-corners elimination match.
note: Billed defending against Soul Stormer and 'Psycho' Cody Hawk at the unaired NBK Pride — no result survives anywhere held. Sources disagree on the date: the fed's own title history gives 18 March 2002, and the 13 March 2002 Wild stages the match; the reign follows the broadcast, and the history's date is kept in the source.

title: chz-heavyweight
label: Matt "The Franchise" Helms

won.source: Caged Fury 2, billed on the 5 March 2003 Wild for the following week, is not among the held shows; on 26 March Helms has "the CHZ World title draped over his shoulder" and says he possesses it "once again" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html).

how: Won the World title at Caged Fury 2; the held shows show him defending it only as a champion.

lost.source: Harry Manback pins him: "we have a new CHZ World heavyweight champion... Harry Manback" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

title: chz-heavyweight
label: Harry Manback

won.source: The no disqualification match with Keyser Soze's interference: "we have a new CHZ World heavyweight champion... Harry Manback" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

how: Beat Matt Helms in a no disqualification match, in place of Keyser Soze, with the Third Reich and a pin.
note: On 21 May 2003 Drayton MacPhereson's pin is counted by a second referee, and Keyser Soze rules that the count does not stand; the first referee raises Manback's hand.

title: chz-heavyweight
label: Gus Theo

won.source: Billed CHZ World Champion on the 5 March 2003 Wild: he "raises the CHZ World title up for the crowd" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-05.html).

how: Champion on 5 March 2003, when he beat Steve Ewing by disqualification in a non-title match; no win is shown on the held shows.

lost.source: Matt Helms holds the title again by the 26 March 2003 Wild (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html); the 5 March Wild bills Caged Fury 2 for the following week, and Gus Theo says he lost his match there.

title: chz-tag-team
label: The AAOD

won.source: The Retribution of Angels and the three count: "The AAOD are the New CHZ tag team champions!!!!!" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

how: Beat Reaper and Archangel in the final of a tag team tournament.
note: The write-up calls the titles reinstated after a tournament "to crown new winners" and names no earlier champion. Retained against Reaper and Archangel on 21 May 2003. The 14 May 2003 booth: "Finally the CHZ's Tag Team titles are reinstated" (may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html). Filed on this belt with the 2003 era's other titles, which carry the fed's 2001-02 belts on (see the title's notes).
